# Appendix B: Drilling, Completions & Fine-Tuning Glossary {#sec-appendix-b .unnumbered}

This glossary supports Chapter 2's training-example builder and every
later chapter's "Engineering Translation" callouts. It is split into two
parts: common oilfield shorthand you'll see in raw report text, and the
fine-tuning/ML vocabulary this book introduces gradually, gathered here
for quick reference. Neither list is exhaustive — abbreviation usage
varies by operator, rig contractor, and basin, and the ML terminology
here is deliberately scoped to what this book actually uses.

| Abbreviation | Expansion |
|---|---|
| AFE | authorization for expenditure |
| BHA | bottom hole assembly |
| BOP | blowout preventer |
| CBL | cement bond log |
| CIRC | circulate |
| COND | condition |
| CSG | casing |

| DFS | days from spud |
| DHSV | downhole safety valve |
| DLS | dogleg severity |
| DOL | days on location |
| DP | drill pipe |

| EMW | equivalent mud weight |
| FIT | formation integrity test |
| FR | from |
| GPM | gallons per minute |
| HWDP | heavy weight drill pipe |
| KOP | kick-off point |
| LOT | leak-off test |
| MD | measured depth |
| MIRU | move in, rig up |
| MW | mud weight |
| MWD | measurement while drilling |
| NMDC | non-magnetic drill collar |
| NPT | non-productive time |
| OBSD | observed |
| PBTD | plugged back total depth |
| PDC | polycrystalline diamond compact (bit type) |
| PJSM | pre-job safety meeting |
| POOH | pull out of hole |
| PPG | pounds per gallon |
| PU | pick up (pipe) |
| PUW | pick up weight |
| RIH | run in hole |
| RKB | rotary kelly bushing |
| ROP | rate of penetration |
| RPM | revolutions per minute |
| SICP | shut-in casing pressure |
| SIDPP | shut-in drill pipe pressure |
| SPP | stand pipe pressure |
| STDS | stands (of drill pipe) |
| TD | total depth |
| TIH | trip in hole |
| TOOH | trip out of hole |
| TVD | true vertical depth |
| WOB | weight on bit |
| WOC | wait on cement |
| WOW | wait on weather |
| XO | crossover (sub) |

::: {.callout-warning title="Abbreviations are not universal"}
The same three letters can mean different things across operators and
basins — build your abbreviation dictionary from *your* archive's actual
usage before trusting it against your own reports.
:::

## B.2 Fine-tuning and local LLM vocabulary

| Term | Plain-language meaning |
|---|---|
| Base model | The general-purpose model before any domain fine-tuning — Chapter 1's starting point. |
| Fine-tuning | Updating a model's weights on your own data so it performs better on your specific task or domain. |
| LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) | A parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that trains a small add-on to the model instead of every weight — Chapter 5's technique. |
| QLoRA | LoRA fine-tuning on a quantized (compressed) copy of the base model, cutting memory needs further. |
| Quantization | Storing a model's weights at lower numerical precision to shrink memory and speed up inference, at some accuracy cost. |
| Checkpoint | A saved snapshot of a model's weights at a point during training — Chapter 8. |
| Tokenizer | The component that splits text into the sub-word units ("tokens") a model actually processes — Chapter 4. |
| Instruction/response pair | A single training example: an instruction (and optional input) paired with the desired output — Chapter 2's core data format. |
| Epoch | One full pass through the training dataset. |
| Perplexity | A numeric measure of how well a model predicts held-out text; lower is generally better — Chapter 11. |
| Hallucination | A fluent but factually unsupported model output — Chapter 10 covers detecting and mitigating it. |
| Drift | A model's behavior changing (often degrading on cases it used to get right) across versions or over time — Chapter 12. |
| RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) | Combining a model with a retrieval step over external documents, instead of relying only on what's in its weights — Chapter 9. |
| Grounded / grounding | An answer that's actually built from a real, cited source, not just retrieved alongside it — Chapter 10 checks the difference. |
| Faithfulness | How well an answer's actual content matches what a specific source says — Chapter 10's word-overlap check is one simple way to measure it. |
